subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A stone is dropped into a quiet lake and the ripples move out in circles at a speed of 5 cm/sec. At the instant when the radius of the circular ripple is 8 cm, how fast is the enclosed area increasing?

mark_split.label: Differentiate A = πr² with respect to t

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you would write, say what the speed of 5 cm/sec is the rate of, and say what you differentiate with respect to.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate A = πr² with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. The speed of the ripple is the rate at which the radius grows, so it is dr/dt and not an area rate. Naming the given and the asked quantity in that form is where this mark sits.
lines: The ripple is a circle whose radius r grows with time.
Given: dr/dt = 5 cm/sec.  Asked: dA/dt when r = 8 cm.
Area enclosed by the ripple:  A = πr²
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That the speed 5 cm/sec is dr/dt, and A = πr² differentiated with respect to t gives dA/dt = 2πr(dr/dt).
accept: the speed of the ripple is the rate of change of the radius
area is pi r squared so d a by d t is two pi r d r by d t
differentiate the area formula with respect to time
ripple speed ante d r by d t, area formula differentiate cheyyali
five centimetres per second is d r by d t
d a by d t equals two pi r into d r by d t

steps.why: Reading the word "speed" as dr/dt is the decision the rest of the answer rests on. Once A = πr² is differentiated with respect to t, the given rate has a place to enter.
common_mistakes: Reading 5 cm/sec as a rate of change of area rather than of radius.
Differentiating πr² as πr or as 2r, losing the π or the factor 2.
Using the circumference 2πr as the area formula.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiating A = πr² gives 2πr, which is the circumference — the area grows along its own boundary, so a wider ripple gains area faster.

steps.label: Substitute r = 8 and dr/dt = 5
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute only after differentiating. Leave the answer as 80π; the decimal value is extra, and the unit cm²/sec must appear.

recall.must_convey: That substituting r = 8 and dr/dt = 5 gives dA/dt = 80π cm²/sec.
accept: substitute r equal to eight and d r by d t equal to five
two pi into eight into five is eighty pi
the area increases at eighty pi square centimetres per second
r equal to eight substitute cheste eighty pi vasthundi
the answer is eighty pi centimetre square per second
about two hundred fifty one square centimetres per second
heard_as: two pi into eight into five

steps.why: The answer depends on r, so it is only the rate at that one instant — a ripple of a different radius gains area at a different rate even at the same speed.
common_mistakes: Substituting r = 8 into A = πr² first, which makes A a fixed number.
Writing the unit as cm/sec instead of cm²/sec.
steps.memory_tip: The answer 80π is 2π × 8 × 5 — the constant, then the radius, then the speed, in the order the formula is written.

insider_note: The ripple is a circle, so A = πr² and dA/dt = 2πr(dr/dt). The speed 5 cm/sec is dr/dt, not dA/dt — reading it as an area rate makes the question unanswerable.
